multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which element most improves reproducibility across two people using the same prompt?

choice.div: An example of good output plus explicit constraints.
A request to "use your best judgment".
A longer prompt with more adjectives.

div.p: Examples and constraints remove interpretation. Adjectives add it.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: When should you stop iterating on a draft?

choice.div: When fixing one point reintroduces another, or the goal can no longer be stated precisely.
When the model says the draft is finished.

div.p: Regression and vagueness are the signals. Take the best draft and edit it yourself.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: What is the highest-risk sentence in an AI-drafted external email?

choice.div: A commitment about timing, money, or outcome that nobody approved.
A greeting that is slightly formal.
A sentence that repeats the customer's own words.

div.p: Style is cheap to fix. An unapproved commitment is a promise the organization must honor.

choice.div: One with a purpose, an example, a test case, a review gate, and a named owner.
One copied from a popular public collection.
One with the longest prompt text.

div.p: Trust comes from documentation and maintenance, not popularity or length.

choiceresponse.p: Which practices keep a shared prompt library healthy? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Placeholders instead of real customer data.
Letting each user edit the canonical prompt freely.

div.p: A library is infrastructure: versioned, owned, tested, and free of real data.
